data.note: claim_classification_map marked complete but body absent from upstream payload; claim types inferred directly from request_text per D7/skill fallback rule

checked_claims.claim_text: 'Layer 2' and 'Layer-2' are architectural layer designators and can be uniformly replaced with the new term 'truth_store' across all documentation.
checked_claims.blocking_condition_if_any: Strong architecture claim asserting Layer 2 = truth_store equivalence; no citation to SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE_AND_BUILD_SEQUENCE_v1.md provided. CLAUDE.md Section 3.1 and Section 3.2 use 'Layer 2' and 'Layer-2' as the canonical designators without establishing 'truth_store' equivalence. Renaming throughout Documentation/ and CLAUDE.md without primary architectural authority constitutes an uncited strong claim.
checked_claims.reason: Architecture equivalence claim (Layer 2 = truth_store) requires explicit primary citation from SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE_AND_BUILD_SEQUENCE_v1.md. None provided. CLAUDE.md itself is constitutional and uses Layer 2 terminology; any assertion that these designators are interchangeable with 'truth_store' must be traced to the architecture document, not inferred.
checked_claims.notes: CLAUDE.md Section 3.1 states 'Layer 2 = operational at snapshot boundary'. Section 3.2 references 'Layer-2 layer2/index_suite.py'. Neither establishes 'truth_store' as an equivalent. Claim cannot be confirmed from available materials. D2 applies: strong claim without role-matched citation -> conflict_requires_block.

checked_claims.claim_text: 'Layer 3' and 'Layer-3' are architectural layer designators and can be uniformly replaced with the new term 'decision_layer' across all documentation.
checked_claims.blocking_condition_if_any: Strong architecture claim asserting Layer 3 = decision_layer equivalence; no citation to SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE_AND_BUILD_SEQUENCE_v1.md provided. CLAUDE.md Section 3.2 lists Layer 3 planned components without defining 'decision_layer' as a synonym. CLAUDE.md Section 3 critical rule and phase gates use 'Layer 3' as the canonical designator.
checked_claims.reason: Architecture equivalence claim (Layer 3 = decision_layer) requires explicit primary citation from SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE_AND_BUILD_SEQUENCE_v1.md. None provided. 'decision_layer' does not appear in available constitutional text as an established synonym. D2 applies.
checked_claims.notes: CLAUDE.md Section 3.2 enumerates planned Layer 3 components (Feature Builder, Index Suite, Regime Gate, Supervisor Engine, Decision Engine, DecisionPacket generator, Execution Layer). None of these are grouped under a 'decision_layer' designator in available materials. The equivalence is asserted, not proven.

checked_claims.claim_text: Code module names, import paths, and unrelated literals must be excluded from the terminology rename.
checked_claims.reason: Protective/limiting constraint, not a strong assertive claim. Directionally consistent with code-conventions.md (explicit imports, no hidden side effects) but SYSTEM_TECHNICAL_HANDBOOK_v1.md is the required primary source for technical constraint claims. code-conventions.md is a rule file, not a canonical document per CLAUDE.md Section 2.1. Citation is partial.
checked_claims.notes: Corroboration is sufficient for review_only given the non-assertive, protective nature of this carve-out. However, primary citation from SYSTEM_TECHNICAL_HANDBOOK_v1.md should be added before any implementation proceeds.

checked_claims.claim_text: README_LAYER2.md filename may require rename handling as part of this terminology refactor.
checked_claims.blocking_condition_if_any: README_LAYER2.md is listed in CLAUDE.md Section 2.1 as a named canonical document in the authoritative documentation set. Its filename is constitutionally anchored. Any rename claim is an architecture + implementation-state claim requiring citations from SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE_AND_BUILD_SEQUENCE_v1.md and SYSTEM_IMPLEMENTATION_RECORD_v1.md. Neither is cited. Furthermore, renaming a canonical document in the CLAUDE.md Section 2.1 list constitutes a constitutional modification requiring governance-level authority, not just a workflow step.
checked_claims.reason: README_LAYER2.md is a constitutionally anchored canonical document name (CLAUDE.md Section 2.1). A rename claim is a strong architecture + implementation claim. No role-matched primary citations provided. D2 and D6 both apply. Mixed claim must be decomposed and each subclaim sourced separately before a passing verdict is possible.
checked_claims.notes: Decomposed subclaims: (a) Architecture subclaim — 'README_LAYER2 name is tied to Layer-2 architectural designation and should be renamed' — requires SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE_AND_BUILD_SEQUENCE_v1.md; uncited -> block. (b) Collaborator workflow subclaim — 'README_LAYER2 role/scope changes with rename' — requires README_LAYER2.md; uncited -> block. (c) Implementation state subclaim — 'rename is safe/non-breaking for all downstream references' — requires SYSTEM_IMPLEMENTATION_RECORD_v1.md; uncited -> block.

checked_claims.claim_text: Historical references must not be blindly altered without governance review.
provided_sources: CLAUDE.md Section 2.3 (historical documents must not be used as current truth — corroborating intent)
checked_claims.reason: Protective constraint. CLAUDE.md Section 2.3 corroborates the intent (historical sources must not be used as current truth, implying they have distinct treatment). Primary source SYSTEM_IMPLEMENTATION_RECORD_v1.md not cited but claim is non-assertive. RC-2 applies.
checked_claims.notes: Citation gap is acceptable for a protective carve-out at review_only level. Full citation from SYSTEM_IMPLEMENTATION_RECORD_v1.md required if this constraint is operationalized as an enforceable rule in any downstream artifact.

checked_claims.claim_text: This terminology refactor applies to CLAUDE.md, which is the constitutional governance document.
checked_claims.blocking_condition_if_any: CLAUDE.md is the constitutional document (highest-priority interpretative authority per its own preamble). Asserting that this workflow has authority to modify CLAUDE.md is a strong governance claim. The upstream governance_context cites workflow_name but does not provide explicit authorization from system-orchestration.yaml for constitutional document modification. CLAUDE.md Section 15 states that governed actions must be subject to orchestration-based workflow enforcement — but modification of the constitution itself requires explicit scope authorization, which is not demonstrated in available materials.
checked_claims.reason: Strong governance claim — asserting workflow authority to modify a constitutional document. Partial citation (workflow name only) is insufficient. Full citation from system-orchestration.yaml establishing CLAUDE.md modification scope is required. D2 applies.
checked_claims.notes: If system-orchestration.yaml explicitly authorizes constitutional document modification within terminology refactor workflows, this claim can be reclassified to RC-1 upon explicit citation. In the absence of that evidence, the claim is blocked.

checked_claims.claim_text: The documentation-wide terminology refactor maintains cross-document consistency across all files in Documentation/ and the canonical set.
checked_claims.blocking_condition_if_any: Strong documentation consistency claim with no citation to DOCUMENTATION_VERIFICATION_MATRIX_v1.md. The claim asserts that post-refactor state will be consistent, but this cannot be verified without consulting the cross-document consistency map. The refactor modifies architectural designators that are cross-referenced throughout the canonical set.
checked_claims.reason: Documentation consistency claims require DOCUMENTATION_VERIFICATION_MATRIX_v1.md as primary source. No citation provided. Without consulting the matrix, cross-document consistency cannot be asserted. D2 applies to this strong current-state claim.
checked_claims.notes: DOCUMENTATION_VERIFICATION_MATRIX_v1.md must be read and cited before any consistency claim can be promoted to compliant status. This is especially critical given that Layer 2/Layer 3 designators appear across multiple canonical documents in the Section 2.1 set.

summary.notes: Five of seven evaluated claims carry conflict_requires_block verdicts. The terminology equivalences (Layer 2 = truth_store, Layer 3 = decision_layer) are the foundational claims upon which the entire refactor depends; both are uncited strong architecture claims. README_LAYER2.md rename is constitutionally anchored and requires decomposed multi-source citation. CLAUDE.md modification scope requires explicit system-orchestration.yaml authorization. No passing verdict can be issued until: (1) SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE_AND_BUILD_SEQUENCE_v1.md is read and explicitly establishes truth_store and decision_layer as equivalent designators; (2) DOCUMENTATION_VERIFICATION_MATRIX_v1.md is consulted for cross-document impact; (3) system-orchestration.yaml is verified to authorize constitutional document modification; (4) SYSTEM_IMPLEMENTATION_RECORD_v1.md confirms rename safety for README_LAYER2.md. Claims C-003 and C-005 (protective carve-outs) are review_only and do not block, but require full primary citations before operationalization.
